post.description:
STOP. A running job is asked to stop itself between items (the threads
pool cannot kill it); a job still queued is revoked and finalised here,
since nothing would ever poll the flag for a task that never runs.

get.description: What Redis and the workers say about themselves right now.

Every team, sorted by parsed maps: the name is what a reader scans for, but
the sample size says whether the page behind it has anything on it.

The match and its maps. ``default_map`` is where a bare match link lands:
the first replayable map, else the first parsed one (whose page can then say
its bundle is gone), else none.

One map: its scene (the floor plan the replay draws on), round list and
scoreboard. The Replay itself was cut from the Tick Data at ingest.

One round's replay payload, sent exactly as stored: gzip JSON, which the
browser decodes on its own (``Content-Encoding: gzip``).

The URL outlives its content (a rebuilt Replay, a map parsed again), so the
browser revalidates every time against an ETag of the stored bytes instead
of trusting a max-age: an unchanged round costs a 304, a changed one is new.

200.description: One round's replay payload (gzip JSON; see app/services/replay.py).

get.description:
Each Team's Summary of the Match, from its Maps' Reviews (built first
where missing or stale). A Map with no Tick Data shows its score only.

The map's Review (CONTEXT.md): every Round's Win probability, Swing and
Findings, worded. Built from the Tick Data on first read after a parse or a
model change, then read back.

Form, numbers by Map and Side, Findings against every Player's, spots, guns.

The Steam id is a string in the path, as everywhere the browser holds one:
as a JavaScript number it would lose its last digits.
Every team with parsed maps, and how many: the picker's list.
Who has played for this team, most recent first: a Lineup's candidates.
Any player by a name they played under: a stand-in or a new signing.
The page header, the tab list and both Lineups, on every tab.
